title: First: sufficient grace suffices for actual conversion
source_text: CXVII. Primo enim cum Molina existimant dari quandam gratiam sufficientem, ad hominis salutem & conversionem, per quam, licet homo actu non convertatur, potest tamen, si voluerit illa uti, actu converti, sine ullo alio praevio Dei auxilio. Nec putant eam gratiam sufficientem recte dici, praeter quam aliud Dei auxilium ad bonam actionem praecedaneum requiritur, ut actio reapse sequatur.
pass_a_gloss: CXVII. For first with Molina they think that there is given a certain sufficient grace, for man's salvation & conversion, by which, although man is not actually converted, he can yet, if he will use it, be actually converted, without any other prior aid of God. Nor do they think that grace rightly called sufficient, beyond which another aid of God going before the good action is required, that the action may really follow.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXVII. First, they hold with Molina that a sufficient grace is given for a person's salvation and conversion. Even if he is not actually converted, he can still be actually converted through it, if he chooses to use it, without any further prior aid from God. A grace that needs some other preceding aid of God before the good action really follows is not, in their view, properly called sufficient.

choices.why: Grace that suffices for actual conversion if the person wills, without further prior aid; kept as in the locus.
